newsitem.title: ZAIRE: South Africa's Mbeki in Zaire for Mobutu talks.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's Mbeki in Zaire for Mobutu talks.

text.p: South Africa's Deputy President Thabo Mbeki arrived in Zaire on Sunday for talks with its beleaguered and ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko, who is the target of a relentless rebel campaign to topple him.

Mobutu, who returned home on Friday to salvage what remains of his authority in the face of fresh rebel advances in the east and south of his sprawling Central African nation, has not been seen in public since leaving France.
Mbeki was at the heart of a bid by South Africa's Nelson Mandela to broker peace between the two sides last month.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila, his popularity soaring with each new battlefield victory, said on Saturday that he would not work with anyone who had shared power with Mobutu.
Kabila outlined his plans for a transitional government during his first visit to Zaire's third city of Kisangani, which the rebels captured on March 15.
He told a news conference a transitional government should include members of his Alliance for Democratic Forces for the Liberation Congo/Zaire (ADFL).
"We say the ADFL transitional government should be made of ADFL members and only anti-Mobutists and anti-regime people who have never been in power and who never shared power," he said.
Any transition, he added, should last no more than a year.

Mobutu, 66, seized power in 1965 but many ordinary Zaireans, eager for a change futh to within 200 km (125 miles) of Zaire's second city Lubumbashi, capital of mineral rich Shaba, and 100 km (60 miles) of the diamond capital of Mbuji-Mayi.
It did not say where exactly they had reached.

The rebels took up arms in October in a dispute about Zairean nationality for an ethnic Tutsi minority, who form the core of Kabila's fighting force. An alliance of anti-Mobutu groups rallied to the cause.
The United States, France and Belgium have sent or are preparing to send troops to countries neighbouring Zaire in anticipation of any need to evacuate their citizens.
Mobutu has spent most of his time in Europe since August when he had prostate cancer surgery there. He left hospital in Monaco on Wednesday after a fresh bout of cancer treatment.
He returned from France on Friday on his private jet but has not been seen in public since boarding the plane in Nice.
Kabila, meanwhile, said he had no personal designs on Zaire's presidency.
"I am not the liberator. I participated in the rebellion, but I don't want to be president," he said. "I want my people to be free and then I will return to my private life."
